mission_06: Excellent work building a comprehensive noise robustness toolkit! You now have multiple complementary approaches for enhancing speech in noisy environments. Spectral subtraction provides a simple, computationally efficient method that works well when a noise-only segment is available for estimation. The Wiener filter offers theoretically optimal noise reduction in the mean-square sense, automatically adjusting the gain at each frequency based on the local SNR. Spectral gating is effective for removing low-level background noise while preserving strong speech components. The ability to add controlled noise at specific SNR levels enables data augmentation for training robust speech recognition models. Understanding these classical signal processing techniques is valuable not only for preprocessing audio before feeding it to neural networks, but also for understanding the frequency-domain operations that modern deep learning-based speech enhancement models learn implicitly. These methods remain relevant in production systems where computational efficiency and interpretability are important.
